title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 14
paragraphs: Mardonius, then, was withdrawing; and when he was already on the road, a message came to him saying that another body of troops, in advance of the rest, had reached Megara — a thousand Lacedaemonians. Being informed of this, he took counsel with himself, wanting if possible to capture these first. So he turned back and began leading his army toward Megara, the cavalry going ahead of the rest and overrunning the Megaran land. This was the furthest point in Europe toward the sunset to which this Persian army came.
